pr_body:
`WindowEmperor` would exit as soon as the last window would enter
`RundownForExit()`, which is too early and triggers leak checks.
This commit splits up the shutdown up into deregistering the window from
the list of windows and into actually decrementing the window count.

Closes #15306

## Validation Steps Performed
* D2D leak warnings seem to disappear ✅

comments:
This happens because this code: https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/10c6206bfef7d045347327687266832931f47eb6/src/cascadia/WindowsTerminal/WindowThread.cpp#L43-L61

is called _after_ we mark the last window as having exited here:
https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/10c6206bfef7d045347327687266832931f47eb6/src/cascadia/WindowsTerminal/WindowEmperor.cpp#L159-L167

This is problematic because once the last window is marked as having exited, we'll send a `WM_QUIT` message to the main thread, which will make Windows Terminal exit sometime soon, potentially before the window thread has actually exited.

But I'm preparing a PR to fix that, and it doesn't actually 100% fix the issue. The `_host = nullptr;` assignment in `RundownForExit()` implicitly destroys the XAML root here, which will make it shut down:
https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/10c6206bfef7d045347327687266832931f47eb6/src/cascadia/WindowsTerminal/IslandWindow.cpp#L40

(`_source` is a `DesktopWindowXamlSource`.) But because WinUI/XAML is a very distinguished system, destroying the `DesktopWindowXamlSource` doesn't actually free any of the XAML elements, like the `TerminalPage`, which is the thing that owns the renderer instance. XAML defers destruction of its objects to some later time (the next render pass?), which only works when the event loop is actually still running. While `RundownForExit()` does continue running the event loop until all messages have been processed, there's absolutely no guarantee that it actually processed _all_ asynchronous messages. After all, some async messages could come in at some point in the far future.
So, sometimes randomly this will still result in none of the XAML objects being released and we'll leak almost all of the window's memory. This is pretty catastrophic, because a) there's no proper fix as far as I'm aware (but if you have more "creative" ideas how we can pump the loop until everything's done, I'd be happy to try it out) and b) Explorer's new tab tearout architecture unknowingly suffers from the exact same bug.
@lhecker Is this that destruction order thing you were talking about during team sync yesterday? Should I put this in 1.18?

review_comments: I made this change because it avoids exposing the innards of `WindowThread`. It's technically unrelated.
